clue.text: Personal appeal from cleaner's mother

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaning lady
the 's is read as a contraction of 'is'
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone's charm is credited to the woman who cleans for them having a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British term for a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling magnetism or charm that draws others to a person.

clue.text: Share bill where daughter leaves cooking apple?

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so this letter is taken out

parts.note: the costard is a large old English cooking apple

explanation.surface: Splitting a restaurant bill when a girl walks out on the stewed fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share bill' reads as splitting a tab but means sharing top billing; the costard is an old English variety of cooking apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-star is to appear as one of the leading performers, sharing top billing.

clue.text: Answer Joycean protagonist having come out

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's novel Ulysses

explanation.surface: An answer concerning the hero of Joyce's novel having revealed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' suggests confessing, but it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Abloom describes a plant in flower, its blossoms having opened.

clue.text: Topless man given peeled carrot

indicators.note: a word made topless loses its first letter

parts.note: Vincent is a man's name

indicators.note: a peeled word has had its outer skin, the first and last letters of given, stripped away

explanation.surface: A shirtless fellow is handed a skinned carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrot' looks like the vegetable being peeled, but it is the definition, in its sense of a reward held out.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot, as in carrot and stick, is a reward offered as an inducement.

clue.text: Entanglement with Amos, Gene and Rita?

definitions.text: Entanglement with Amos, Gene and Rita?

indicators.note: an entanglement is a twisted-up mess, so these names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three people named Amos, Gene and Rita getting mixed up together.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a romantic entanglement involving three people.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage à trois is a domestic arrangement in which three people share a sexual relationship.

clue.text: Car getting bashed to avoid marks?

parts.note: to dodge something is to avoid it
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A car being knocked about, apparently so as to escape getting dents or scratches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like scratches on paintwork, but it is the currency abbreviated to M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a small electric fairground car that riders deliberately bump into one another.

clue.text: Zombie oath used regularly in Caribbean sorcery

indicators.note: letters used regularly are taken at even intervals, every other one of Zombie oath

explanation.surface: A zombie's oath turns up regularly in tales of West Indian magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of folk magic and witchcraft practised in the West Indies.

clue.text: Willing to forgive corrupt surgeon smuggling in ecstasy

indicators.note: smuggling in means carrying something hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other
corrupt means twisted or debased, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A crooked doctor sneaks drugs in, yet someone is ready to pardon them.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous person is magnanimous, ready to overlook faults and pardon others.

clue.text: Swallow meat regularly for disciplinarian

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters, here the second and fourth of meat

explanation.surface: A command to gulp down meat routinely, as a strict taskmaster might issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about eating meat, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules, named after a severe French drillmaster.

clue.text: Say senseless crook close to treasure — is it seen in large chest?

definitions.text: is it seen in large chest?

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as spoken, and only its sound counts

parts.note: senseless means silly
a con, short for convict or con man, is a crook

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of treasure

explanation.surface: A daft swindler near a hoard asks whether something might be hidden in a big trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' makes SILLY spoken sound like the first letters SILI. 'Large chest' is not a treasure chest but an enhanced bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone gel is the material of many breast implants, which make for a larger bust.

clue.text: Note Caruso perhaps articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was a celebrated operatic tenor, so he is an example of one

explanation.surface: A remark about how the great singer Caruso might have pronounced something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical alongside Caruso, but it is a banknote: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is the everyday British word for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Motown maestro direct about idea on Detroit to start with

indicators.note: about means going around, so the synonym for direct encloses the rest

parts.note: to direct a vehicle is to steer it
a view is an opinion or idea

indicators.note: to start with picks the first letter of Detroit

explanation.surface: An instruction to guide a music label's thinking toward Detroit, its home city.
explanation.walkthrough: Motown Records was founded in Detroit, so the surface stays in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevie Wonder is one of the most celebrated artists on the Motown record label.

clue.text: Decorate with regular picks from garden?

wordplay.reading: alternate letters of GARDEN, joined as choices by OR

parts.note: every other letter of garden is taken, and 'picks' adds the sense of choosing between those letters, with the word for choosing between them written in

explanation.surface: Brightening a room with flowers picked at regular intervals in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of gArDeN are A, D and N; read as 'picks' (choices) they become A, D OR N, so the OR is part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to embellish or beautify it with ornaments.

clue.text: Hair-to-rug transformation seen in spin supremo?

indicators.note: a transformation changes a thing's form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning hair into a rug, as might be witnessed in the hands of a master of spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Guto Harri was Boris Johnson's director of communications in Downing Street in 2022, hence a 'spin supremo'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prime minister's communications chief, Harri was a leading political spin doctor.

clue.text: Plug hole in motorway certain to produce accident

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main north–south motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces are put inside the following ones

parts.note: certain means sure
a plug is an advertisement, an ad
a vent is a hole letting air or smoke out

explanation.surface: Blocking a gap in a motorway is bound to cause a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' and 'hole' look like a road repair, but each is a synonym; 'in' sends both inside. The M1 is the main motorway from London to Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is an unlucky mishap; death by misadventure is an accidental death.

clue.text: Final character in set troubled revolutionary philosopher

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: The last letter in a group is disturbed by a radical thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like an insertion signal but is part of the anagram fodder with the Z. Che Guevara was the Argentine Marxist revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Nietzsche was a nineteenth-century German thinker known for the idea of the Übermensch.

clue.text: Old Roman god guards unknown ship for hero

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: deus is the Latin word for god
Y is an algebraic unknown
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman deity keeps watch over a mystery vessel for a heroic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Odysseus, whom the Romans called Ulysses, is the hero of Homer's Odyssey; the ship suits his long voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the wandering Greek hero of Homer's epic poem the Odyssey.

clue.text: Waves and cheers to welcome star on unfinished film

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next part
to welcome is to take in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers
the sun is a star

indicators.note: unfinished means its last letter is missing

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: Fans wave and cheer to greet a celebrity at the premiere of an incomplete movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves and cheers' reads as a crowd's welcome, but 'Waves' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea waves triggered by earthquakes or underwater landslides.

clue.text: Crestfallen heir ends date explosively

indicators.note: something blown apart explosively lands in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disappointed heir breaks off a romantic date in a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen and disheartened both describe someone dejected after a setback.

clue.text: Sailor worried and died — sank?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: A sailor fretted and perished: did his ship go down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sank' suggests a ship, but it means subsided; the question mark flags the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Abated means lessened or subsided, as a storm dies down and sinks to calm.

clue.text: Hydra moving across lake only with great difficulty

indicators.note: across means spanning something, so the rearranged letters straddle the other piece
moving means shifting around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The many-headed monster struggles to cross a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent slain by Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly in its older sense means with hardship, barely managed.

clue.text: Country moans — rain all over the place!

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are jumbled, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation complains that it is raining everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Seconds refused, sandwich for Schwarzenegger?

indicators.note: refused means rejected, so this letter is turned away

parts.note: sarnie is British slang for a sandwich

explanation.surface: Someone declines another helping of a sandwich, perhaps a bodybuilder on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is everyday British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnie is the popular nickname of actor Arnold Schwarzenegger, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Much enthusiasm about brother's wild horse

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other
much of a word is most of it, so the last letter of the synonym for enthusiasm goes

parts.note: zeal is fervent enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Lots of excitement surrounding a sibling's untamed horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' trims ZEAL to ZEA, which goes 'about' BR.
explanation.definitionFit: The zebra is a striped African equid, a wild relative of the domestic horse.

clue.text: Fur coat taken from Vera — by Tees?

indicators.note: removing a word's coat strips its outer letters, leaving only the middle of Vera

parts.note: Tees is this puzzle's setter, so something by Tees is the setter's: mine

explanation.surface: A fur coat has been stolen from a woman called Vera, perhaps somewhere along the River Tees.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the setter's pseudonym and also a river in north-east England, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine is the white winter pelt of the stoat, a prized fur for robes.

clue.text: Learned river ebbs to cover old coin

indicators.note: to cover something is to go around it, so one piece encloses the other
a river that ebbs flows back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe in former times

explanation.surface: A river's falling tide comes to cover an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ebbs' suits a river and signals reading it backwards. The Dee flows through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned as an adjective means well schooled, as an educated person is.

clue.text: Security emptied trunk in procedure

indicators.note: a word emptied loses its contents, leaving only the first and last letters of Security

parts.note: a stem is the main stalk or trunk of a plant

explanation.surface: Security staff empty out a car boot or suitcase as part of standard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or set of steps for doing something.

clue.text: Intimate insect devours distressed diner

indicators.note: devours means swallows up, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: distressed means upset or knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bug eats a diner who is already upset, rather too closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate as an adjective describes a close, warm relationship, as friendly does.
